causes.text: Intel said it would invest $20 billion to build two semiconductor fabrication plants in Ohio, a project aimed at producing advanced chips and reducing reliance on Asian manufacturing.

source_info.title: Intel announces plans for an investment of more than $28 billion for two new chip factories in Licking County, Ohio.

effects.text: Apple reported earnings that exceeded analysts expectations but cautioned that ongoing supply chain constraints could cost the company $48 billion, leading its shares to decline and leaving them roughly 100% lower year to date.

source_info.title: Apple Expects Supply Shortages to Slash Sales by Up to $8 Billion

causal_reasoning_chain.description: On 2022-01-21, Intel's $20 billion investment in U.S. chip plants underscored structural semiconductor shortages, with new capacity expected only in the long term.
Apple was already experiencing severe component delays and warned of financial risks from ongoing supply constraints.
On 2022-04-29, Despite strong quarterly earnings, the forecasted $48 billion supply hit caused Apple shares to fall significantly. The move was 3.66%.

rationale: Intel's investment confirmed the persistence of chip supply bottlenecks. Apple, deeply integrated into the global supply chain, anticipated major revenue losses, which spooked investors and led to a notable share price decline.
counterfactual_analysis: If Intel factories had already been operational and chip supply normalized, Apple supply constraints may have been mitigated, possibly avoiding the stock drop following earnings.

adversarial_confounders.impact: May have amplified stock declines across tech firms

adversarial_confounders.text: Interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve
adversarial_confounders.impact: Created macro pressure on growth stocks

adversarial_confounders.text: Investors taking profits after a long rally
adversarial_confounders.impact: Could explain part of the drop regardless of supply news

details.commentary: Ongoing U.S.-China trade tensions and export controls encouraged Apple to diversify its production footprint beyond mainland China. As the company gradually shifted more assembly to India, investor expectations for supply-chain resilience and political risk mitigation fed back into stronger confidence after successful launches.

details.pestel_factor: Political - Trade tensions and industrial policy shaped Apple's manufacturing choices
details.commentary: U.S. export restrictions and geopolitical friction made heavy reliance on Chinese manufacturing increasingly risky for Apple. Supportive policies in India and a desire to reduce exposure to sanctions created a politically driven incentive to move more production, which investors rewarded once execution became visible.
